final_answer:
The performance of ablated versions of LightRAG was evaluated using four variants: -High (removing high-level retrieval), -Low (removing low-level retrieval), -Origin (using only graph-based indexing without original text), and the full version, LightRAG. The results are presented in Table 2 of the source document.

- **Low-level-only Retrieval (-High variant)**: This variant removes high-level retrieval and experiences a significant performance decline across nearly all datasets and metrics. For example, in the "Comprehensiveness" metric for the Agriculture dataset, the -High variant scores 65.2% compared to 67.6% for the full LightRAG [1]. The drop is attributed to the overemphasis on specific entities and their immediate neighbors, limiting the ability to address complex queries requiring comprehensive insights [4].

- **High-level-only Retrieval (-Low variant)**: This variant prioritizes a broader range of content by leveraging entity-wise relationships but lacks depth in specific entity analysis. For instance, in the "Empowerment" metric for the Legal dataset, the -Low variant scores 83.6%, while LightRAG scores 83.6% as well, but the -Low variant may struggle with precise, detailed answers [1]. This trade-off results in strong comprehensiveness but reduced depth [4].

- **Hybrid Mode (Full LightRAG)**: The full version of LightRAG combines the strengths of both low-level and high-level retrieval, achieving balanced performance across multiple dimensions. For example, in the "Overall" metric for the CS dataset, LightRAG scores 61.2%, significantly outperforming -High (56.0%) and -Low (56.4%) [1]. This dual-level approach ensures both breadth and depth in data analysis [4].

- **Semantic Graph Indexing (-Origin variant)**: The -Origin variant eliminates the use of original text and relies solely on graph-based indexing. Surprisingly, it does not exhibit significant performance declines and shows improvements in some cases, such as the "Comprehensiveness" metric for the Agriculture dataset (75.2% for -Origin vs. 67.6% for LightRAG) [1]. This is attributed to the effective extraction of key information during graph-based indexing, which reduces noise from irrelevant text [4].

In conclusion, the ablation studies demonstrate that the hybrid mode of LightRAG, which integrates low-level and high-level retrieval, performs best overall. Variants that remove one retrieval level or rely solely on graph-based indexing show either reduced performance or specific trade-offs in depth or comprehensiveness [1][4].
